summary: Benjamin A. Elman is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under Nathan Sivin and Susan Naquin. He held posts at UCLA (1986–2002) and Princeton University (2002).

Benjamin Bogin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr., and also studied under Janet Gyatso, Gareth Sparham, and Lopon Ugyen Rinpoche.

Benjamin Brose specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his Ph.D. at Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, later serving as assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan (~2009–2017).

Benjamin C. Ray is a religious studies scholar. He has held positions at the University of Virginia, including Daniels Family NEH Distinguished Teaching Professor in the Department of Religious Studies (attested 2000) and faculty member (attested 2026).
Benjamin Goldstein is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. As of 2026, he is a PhD Candidate in Religious Studies at McMaster University, studying under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke.
Benjamin Luk Williams works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. from Harvard University in 2017 and held a post at Naropa University.

Benjamin W. Fortson IV specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Yale University (~1985–1989) and Harvard University (~1991–1996), and held a post at the University of Michigan around 2005.

Benjamin Wood specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Toronto under Frances Garrett, and also studied with Khenpo Kunga Sherab, Thupten Champa, and Shayne Clarke.

Benkyo Shiio was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo in 1915. He lectured at Taisho, Nihon, and Waseda universities, and served as head of the Sanko Library, Sanko Research Institute, and Tokai Gakuen University Junior College.

Benoytosh Bhattacharyya was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Calcutta and the University of Dhaka, and served as Director at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda beginning in 1927.

Benoît Vermander is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He studied at Yale, Sciences Po, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Centre Sèvres. He served as Academic Director at the Taipei Ricci Institute (1996–2009) and professor at Fudan University (2009).

Bernard Faure specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his Doctorat d'État at the University of Paris/Paris Diderot, and held professorships at Cornell (~1983–1987), Stanford (~1987–2006), and Columbia University (~2006–2021).

Bernard Frank was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. He served as head of the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1972–1974) and held the chair of Civilisation japonaise at the Collège de France (1979–1996).

Bernard Williams was a philosopher who studied at Balliol College, Oxford (~1947–1951). He held academic posts at University College London (~1964–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1988–2003).
Bernd Schneidmüller is a historian who held academic posts at the University of Oldenburg (~1987–1992) and Heidelberg University (~2003).

Bernfried Schlerath was an Iranian, Central Asian, linguistics, and Indology scholar who studied under Paul Thieme. He held posts at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1959–1971), University of Marburg (~1966–1974), and Free University of Berlin (~1974–1992).
Bernhard Breloer was an Indology scholar who served as a professor at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1937 to 1945, succeeding Heinrich Lüders.

Bernhard Forssman is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, linguistics, and Indology. He studied under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, holding posts at the University of Marburg (1968–1983) and Erlangen-Nuremberg (1983).

Bernhard Geiger was an Indology and Iranian studies scholar who studied at Vienna, Bonn, Charles, Göttingen, and Heidelberg. He held posts at the University of Vienna (~1909–1938), the Iranian Institute (1938–1951), and Columbia University (1951–1953).

Bernhard Hirzel was an Indology scholar who studied at Zurich, Berlin under Franz Bopp, Göttingen, and Paris. He held teaching posts as reader, Dozent, and Privatdozent at the University of Zurich between 1833 and 1845.
